``` {r bates-engine}
# ==============================================================================
# 4. Stage 1 Engine: Bates (2015) Five-Step Random-Structure Selection
#    Combined with Alday (2019) baseline-as-covariate fixed-effect specification.
# ==============================================================================
#
# FIXED-EFFECT SPECIFICATION (face phase, single-factor emotion)
# Under Alday: the pairwise model (emotion + Baseline_c)^2 serves as the search
# space; the buildmer 'include' argument forces retention of emotion and
# Baseline_c, while the emotion:Baseline_c interaction is subjected to LRT-based
# inclusion testing (data-driven Alday). Under traditional baseline subtraction:
# the fixed model is simply emotion (no baseline covariate).
#
# RANDOM-EFFECT STRUCTURE (Bates 2015 / Matuschek 2017 five-step pipeline)
#   Step 1: Design-justified maximal model with the by-subject emotion random
#           slope and its correlation with the intercept: (1 + emotion | id).
#           (Face phase has one within-subject factor, emotion.)
#   Step 2: Zero-correlation-parameter (ZCP) model as fallback starting point
#           for variance-component selection.
#   Step 3: LRT-based backward elimination via buildmer (alpha = 0.20 per
#           Matuschek et al. 2017, equivalent to AIC for nested two-model
#           comparisons; avoids the over-conservative model selection that
#           strict alpha = 0.05 would impose at this stage).
#   Step 4: Test whether adding correlation parameters improves fit, by
#           enumerating candidate correlated structures over the surviving
#           variance components and selecting via LRT/AIC.
#   Step 5: rePCA diagnostic on the final model documents the dimensionality
#           supported by the data, written to the reproducibility log.
# ==============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: parse a fitted model's formula to identify which random slopes
# survived Step 3. Returns a character vector of slope variable names.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
extract_surviving_slopes <- function(model) {
  re_terms <- lme4::findbars(formula(model))
  surviving <- character(0)
  for (term in re_terms) {
    rhs <- deparse(term[[2]])
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*0\\s*\\+\\s*", "", rhs)
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*1\\s*\\+\\s*", "", rhs)
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*1\\s*$",       "", rhs)
    rhs <- trimws(rhs)
    if (rhs == "" || rhs == "1") next
    parts <- trimws(strsplit(rhs, "\\+")[[1]])
    surviving <- c(surviving, parts)
  }
  unique(surviving)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: rePCA dimensionality summary as a tidy data frame, one row per
# principal component with cumulative variance explained.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
extract_repca_summary <- function(model, group_name = "participant_id") {
  # Defensive: rePCA() requires a merMod object; lm or lmerTest objects without
  # the underlying lme4 slot will trigger getME() failures. Return an NA frame
  # so downstream count_effective_dims() returns NA cleanly.
  if (!inherits(model, "merMod")) {
    return(data.frame(component = NA_integer_, sd = NA_real_,
                      proportion_variance = NA_real_,
                      cumulative_variance = NA_real_))
  }
  pca_obj <- tryCatch(lme4::rePCA(model), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(pca_obj) || !group_name %in% names(pca_obj)) {
    return(data.frame(component = NA_integer_, sd = NA_real_,
                      proportion_variance = NA_real_,
                      cumulative_variance = NA_real_))
  }
  imp <- summary(pca_obj[[group_name]])$importance
  data.frame(
    component = seq_len(ncol(imp)),
    sd = imp["Standard deviation", ],
    proportion_variance = imp["Proportion of Variance", ],
    cumulative_variance = imp["Cumulative Proportion", ]
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: count effective dimensions (those reaching >= threshold cumulative
# variance). Indicates whether the random structure is overparameterized.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
count_effective_dims <- function(repca_df, threshold = 0.999) {
  if (all(is.na(repca_df$cumulative_variance))) return(NA_integer_)
  hit <- which(repca_df$cumulative_variance >= threshold)
  if (length(hit) == 0) nrow(repca_df) else hit[1]
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 4 helper: enumerate candidate correlated structures over surviving
# variance components, fit each, and select via LRT vs. ZCP (alpha = 0.20 per
# Matuschek et al. 2017). Returns the best-fitting model with REML refitted
# for inference.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_correlations_step4 <- function(model_zcp_reduced, fixed_str, data, alpha_lrt = 0.20) {
  # Defensive: if the reduced model is not an lme4 mixed model (e.g. degraded
  # to plain lm during Step 3), there are no random slopes to add correlations
  # to. Return as-is.
  if (!inherits(model_zcp_reduced, "merMod")) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] Reduced model is not a mixed model; skipping correlation tests.",
                 indent = 1)
    return(model_zcp_reduced)
  }
  
  surviving <- extract_surviving_slopes(model_zcp_reduced)
  
  if (length(surviving) == 0) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] Reduced model has only random intercept; no correlations to test.",
                 indent = 1)
    # SAFETY: do NOT use update(model_zcp_reduced, REML = TRUE). When
    # model_zcp_reduced was extracted from buildmer (bm_res@model), its
    # @call slot stores buildmer's internal data placeholder ('..2'),
    # not the actual data argument. update.merMod tries to re-evaluate
    # the call in the current environment, where '..2' does not exist,
    # producing "bad 'data': ..2 used in an incorrect context".
    # Explicit refit using formula(model) and the function's `data`
    # argument bypasses this issue.
    f_zcp_only <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
    return(lme4::lmer(f_zcp_only, data = data, REML = TRUE,
                      control = custom_control))
  }
  
  # Build candidate set. ZCP-baseline always included for LRT baseline.
  candidates <- list()
  candidates[["ZCP_baseline"]] <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
  
  # All-correlated candidate: (1 + s1 + s2 + ... | id)
  all_str <- paste(surviving, collapse = " + ")
  candidates[["All_correlated"]] <- as.formula(
    paste(fixed_str, "+ (1 +", all_str, "| participant_id)")
  )
  
  # Pairwise candidates: intercept correlated with one slope at a time.
  if (length(surviving) > 1) {
    for (i in seq_along(surviving)) {
      others <- setdiff(surviving, surviving[i])
      if (length(others) > 0) {
        others_terms <- paste(
          sprintf("(0 + %s | participant_id)", others),
          collapse = " + "
        )
        cand_str <- paste(fixed_str,
                          sprintf("+ (1 + %s | participant_id)", surviving[i]),
                          "+", others_terms)
      } else {
        cand_str <- paste(fixed_str,
                          sprintf("+ (1 + %s | participant_id)", surviving[i]))
      }
      candidates[[paste0("Int_with_", surviving[i])]] <- as.formula(cand_str)
    }
  }
  
  # Fit each candidate under ML for valid LRT comparison.
  total_cands <- length(candidates)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] Fitting %d candidate correlated structures...",
                       total_cands), indent = 1)
  fits <- list()
  cand_idx <- 0
  for (nm in names(candidates)) {
    cand_idx <- cand_idx + 1
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] Trying '%s'...",
                         cand_idx, total_cands, nm), indent = 2)
    t_cand <- Sys.time()
    fit <- tryCatch(
      lme4::lmer(candidates[[nm]], data = data, REML = FALSE,
                 control = custom_control_final),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    fit_diag <- if (is.null(fit)) NULL else final_lmm_diagnostics(fit)
    if (!is.null(fit) && isTRUE(fit_diag$valid)) {
      fits[[nm]] <- fit
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' converged (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    } else if (!is.null(fit)) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' invalid; excluded (%s): %s",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand),
                           format_final_lmm_diagnostics(fit_diag)),
                   indent = 3)
    } else {
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' failed to converge (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    }
  }
  
  if (is.null(fits[["ZCP_baseline"]])) {
    stop(
      "[Step 4] The buildmer-selected ZCP reference failed the mandatory ",
      "acceptance gate. Correlated candidates cannot be selected without the ",
      "prespecified LRT reference; stopping for explicit review."
    )
  }
  
  if (length(fits) == 1) {
    # Only ZCP_baseline survived (others singular). Keep it.
    progress_log("[Step 4] Only ZCP candidate viable; correlations not added.", indent = 1)
    # See safety note above re: update() and buildmer-derived models.
    f_zcp_only <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
    m_zcp_only <- lme4::lmer(f_zcp_only, data = data, REML = TRUE,
                             control = custom_control_final)
    attr(m_zcp_only, "step4_selected") <- "ZCP_baseline"
    return(m_zcp_only)
  }
  
  # ZCP_baseline is the prespecified reference because all richer candidates are
  # nested within it. It has already passed the same mandatory acceptance gate.
  # NOTE: "baseline" here refers to the Step 4 reference model, NOT to the
  # pre-stimulus EEG baseline (Baseline_c). The two are unrelated.
  baseline_fit <- fits[["ZCP_baseline"]]
  lrt_table <- data.frame(model = character(), df_diff = integer(),
                          chisq = numeric(), p_value = numeric(),
                          AIC = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  best_name <- "ZCP_baseline"
  best_fit  <- baseline_fit

  for (nm in setdiff(names(fits), "ZCP_baseline")) {
    cand <- fits[[nm]]
    lrt <- tryCatch(anova(baseline_fit, cand), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(lrt) || nrow(lrt) < 2) next
    
    p_val <- lrt$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2]
    if (is.na(p_val)) next
    
    lrt_table <- rbind(lrt_table, data.frame(
      model = nm,
      df_diff = lrt$Df[2],
      chisq = lrt$Chisq[2],
      p_value = p_val,
      AIC = AIC(cand),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))

    # Select candidate with lowest AIC among those passing alpha_lrt.
    if (p_val < alpha_lrt && AIC(cand) < AIC(best_fit)) {
      best_name <- nm
      best_fit  <- cand
    }
  }
  
  attr(best_fit, "step4_lrt_table") <- lrt_table
  attr(best_fit, "step4_selected") <- best_name
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] Selected: %s (alpha_LRT = %.2f).",
                       best_name, alpha_lrt), indent = 1)
  
  f_best <- formula(best_fit)
  m_reml <- lme4::lmer(f_best, data = data, REML = TRUE,
                       control = custom_control_final)
  for (an in c("step4_lrt_table", "step4_selected")) {
    a <- attr(best_fit, an)
    if (!is.null(a)) attr(m_reml, an) <- a
  }
  m_reml
}

# ==============================================================================
# Main Stage 1 engine: full Bates 5-step pipeline + Alday 2.5 fixed structure.
# Returns the fitted model with diagnostic attributes attached.
# ==============================================================================
fit_stage1_bates <- function(data, erp_name) {
  
  # Face phase: emotion is the sole design factor. Fixed-effect specification
  # branches on the method toggle:
  #   Alday (use_baseline_covariate = TRUE): (emotion + Baseline_c)^2, i.e.
  #     emotion + Baseline_c + emotion:Baseline_c. The emotion:Baseline_c
  #     interaction is LRT-tested (not forced) per data-driven Alday.
  #   Traditional (FALSE): emotion only (amplitude already baseline-corrected).
  if (use_baseline_covariate) {
    fixed_str <- sprintf("%s ~ (emotion + Baseline_c)^2", erp_name)
    fixed_include <- as.formula("~ emotion + Baseline_c + (1 | participant_id)")
  } else {
    fixed_str <- sprintf("%s ~ emotion", erp_name)
    fixed_include <- as.formula("~ emotion + (1 | participant_id)")
  }
  random_design <- add_random_contrast_columns(
    data, "emotion", "participant_id"
  )
  data <- random_design$data
  # Forced-include set for buildmer Step 3: the core emotion term (and, under
  # Alday, Baseline_c) must remain regardless of LRT outcome. The by-subject
  # random intercept is also forced because it reflects the nested data
  # structure (trials within subjects); without it, single-trial EEG data are
  # pseudo-replicated and inference is invalid.
  
  diag_log <- list(
    component = erp_name,
    n_obs = nrow(data),
    n_subjects = dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id),
    random_contrast_columns = random_design$random_columns,
    random_slope_blocks = unique(unname(random_design$random_blocks)),
    step1_status = NA_character_,
    step1_pca = NULL,
    step2_status = NA_character_,
    step3_final_formula = NA_character_,
    step4_status = NA_character_,
    step5_pca = NULL
  )
  
  # ---- STEP 1: Barr-style maximal model (main-effects random slopes only). ----
  progress_log(sprintf("[%s] Stage 1: Bates 5-step random-structure selection",
                       erp_name))
  progress_log(sprintf("Data: N = %d trials, %d subjects.",
                       nrow(data), dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id)),
               indent = 1)
  
  random_max <- sprintf(
    "(1 + %s | participant_id)",
    paste(random_design$random_columns, collapse = " + ")
  )
  f_max <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+", random_max))
  
  progress_log("[Step 1] Fitting design-justified maximal model with correlations...",
               indent = 1)
  t_step1 <- Sys.time()
  m_max <- tryCatch(
    R.utils::withTimeout(
      lme4::lmer(f_max, data = data, REML = FALSE, control = custom_control),
      timeout = 300,
      onTimeout = "error"
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[WARN] Maximal diagnostic failed or timed out: %s",
                           conditionMessage(e)),
                   indent = 2)
      NULL
    }
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 1] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step1)),
               indent = 2)
  
  if (!is.null(m_max)) {
    is_sing <- lme4::isSingular(m_max, tol = 1e-4)
    diag_log$step1_status <- if (is_sing) "converged_singular" else "converged_clean"
    diag_log$step1_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_max)
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 1] Status: %s. Effective dims = %d / %d.",
                         diag_log$step1_status,
                         count_effective_dims(diag_log$step1_pca),
                         nrow(diag_log$step1_pca)),
                 indent = 2)
  } else {
    diag_log$step1_status <- "diagnostic_failed_or_timed_out"
  }
  
  # ---- STEP 2: Zero-correlation-parameter (ZCP) model. ----
  progress_log("[Step 2] Fitting zero-correlation-parameter model...", indent = 1)
  t_step2 <- Sys.time()
  
  random_zcp <- paste(
    c("(1 | participant_id)", random_design$random_terms),
    collapse = " + "
  )
  f_zcp <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+", random_zcp))
  blocked_terms <- make_blocked_buildmer_terms(
    f_zcp, random_design$random_blocks
  )
  
  m_zcp <- tryCatch(
    lme4::lmer(f_zcp, data = data, REML = FALSE, control = custom_control),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 2] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step2)), indent = 2)
  
  if (is.null(m_zcp)) {
    progress_log("[Step 2] Contrast-coded ZCP diagnostic fit failed; continuing to buildmer ordering.",
                 indent = 2)
    diag_log$step2_status <- "failed"
  } else {
    is_sing_zcp <- lme4::isSingular(m_zcp, tol = 1e-4)
    diag_log$step2_status <- if (is_sing_zcp) "converged_singular" else "converged_clean"
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 2] Status: %s.", diag_log$step2_status), indent = 2)
  }
  
  # ---- STEP 3: LRT-based backward elimination via buildmer. ----
  # buildmer drops both fixed-effect baseline interactions and random-effect
  # variance components if not supported by data. Theoretical core terms are
  # protected by the 'include' argument.
  #
  # Elimination criterion uses alpha = 0.20 per Matuschek, Kliegl, Vasishth,
  # Baayen, & Bates (2017, Journal of Memory and Language). Their simulations
  # showed that alpha = 0.05 over-penalizes model complexity at the elimination
  # stage, sacrificing power to detect true fixed effects. Alpha = 0.20 is
  # approximately equivalent to AIC-based selection for nested two-model
  # comparisons and provides the optimal Type I error / power tradeoff for
  # typical psychological / psycholinguistic datasets.
  #
  # Note on buildmer API: 'crit' governs term ordering (default LRT), while
  # 'elim' governs elimination decisions. LRTalpha() generates an elimination
  # function and must be passed to 'elim', not 'crit'.
  progress_log("[Step 3] LRT-based backward elimination (buildmer, alpha = 0.20)...",
               indent = 1)
  progress_log(paste("This step iteratively tests model terms via LRT and may fit",
                     "many candidate models. With large N (>20,000 trials) and",
                     "complex random structures, expect several minutes per",
                     "component. buildmer's internal progress is shown below."),
               indent = 2)
  progress_log("[Step 3] Engineering protections active: lmerTest detached during",
               indent = 2)
  progress_log("buildmer call; withTimeout=1800s; stop on selection failure.",
               indent = 2)
  t_step3 <- Sys.time()
  
  bm_ctrl <- buildmer::buildmerControl(
    dep = erp_name,
    include = fixed_include,
    direction = c("order", "backward"),
    crit = "LRT",
    elim = buildmer::LRTalpha(0.20),
    quiet = FALSE,
    args = list(control = custom_control)
    # Note: REML is managed by buildmer internally based on whether the
    # comparison is between fixed-effect or random-effect changes. Passing
    # REML here causes a duplicate-argument error.
  )
  
  bm_res <- run_buildmer_protected(
    buildmer::buildmer,
    formula = blocked_terms, data = data,
    buildmerControl = bm_ctrl,
    timeout_sec = 1800
  )
  
  if (is.null(bm_res)) {
    stop("Step 3 buildmer selection failed or timed out; no unvalidated ",
         "ZCP fallback will be reported.")
  } else {
    m_reduced <- tryCatch({
      bm_res@model
    }, error = function(e) {
      stop("Could not extract the buildmer-selected model: ",
           conditionMessage(e))
    })
  }
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 3] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step3)), indent = 2)
  
  # Sanity check: buildmer can occasionally eliminate ALL random-effect terms,
  # returning a plain `lm` object. Single-trial EEG analysis without random
  # intercepts is invalid (pseudo-replication of trials within subjects), so we
  # rebuild the minimum viable LMM with a random intercept. This branch should
  # be rare given that (1 | participant_id) is in the include set above.
  if (!inherits(m_reduced, "merMod")) {
    progress_log("[WARN] Reduced model lost all random effects; refitting with (1 | participant_id).",
                 indent = 2)
    reduced_fixed_str_recovered <- paste(deparse(formula(m_reduced)), collapse = " ")
    f_recover <- as.formula(paste(reduced_fixed_str_recovered, "+ (1 | participant_id)"))
    m_reduced <- lme4::lmer(f_recover, data = data, REML = FALSE,
                            control = custom_control)
  }
  
  diag_log$step3_final_formula <- paste(deparse(formula(m_reduced)), collapse = " ")
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 3] Reduced formula: %s",
                       stringr::str_squish(diag_log$step3_final_formula)),
               indent = 2)
  
  # ---- STEP 4: Test correlation parameters on surviving slopes. ----
  progress_log("[Step 4] Testing correlation parameters on surviving slopes...",
               indent = 1)
  t_step4 <- Sys.time()
  
  # Reconstruct fixed-only formula from the reduced model for Step 4 candidates.
  reduced_fixed <- nobars(formula(m_reduced))
  reduced_fixed_str <- paste(deparse(reduced_fixed), collapse = " ")
  
  m_final <- add_correlations_step4(m_reduced, reduced_fixed_str, data, alpha_lrt = 0.20)
  diag_log$step4_status <- attr(m_final, "step4_selected") %||% "ZCP_kept"
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] elapsed: %s. Selected: %s.",
                       format_elapsed(t_step4), diag_log$step4_status),
               indent = 2)
  
  # ---- STEP 5: rePCA diagnostic on final model. ----
  diag_log$step5_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_final)
  step5_eff <- count_effective_dims(diag_log$step5_pca)
  step5_nom <- nrow(diag_log$step5_pca)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 5] Final model dimensionality: %s effective / %s nominal.",
                       if (is.na(step5_eff)) "NA" else as.character(step5_eff),
                       if (is.na(step5_nom)) "NA" else as.character(step5_nom)),
               indent = 1)
  
  # ---- Defensive REML guard. ----
  # 
  # Several paths through add_correlations_step4 and fit_stage1_bates can
  # return an LMM in ML state (REML=FALSE). lmerTest::anova(ddf="Satterthwaite")
  # expects REML by default. Refit REML here unconditionally so the downstream
  # ANOVA cascade has a clean input.
  # 
  # SAFETY: do NOT use update() because m_final may be a buildmer @model
  # object whose @call references buildmer's internal '..2' placeholder,
  # which fails outside buildmer's scope. Refit explicitly from formula
  # and the local `data` argument.
  if (inherits(m_final, "merMod")) {
    is_reml <- tryCatch(lme4::isREML(m_final), error = function(e) FALSE)
    if (!isTRUE(is_reml)) {
      progress_log("[Final] Refitting LMM with REML=TRUE for Satterthwaite compatibility.",
                   indent = 1)
      f_final <- formula(m_final)
      m_final_reml <- tryCatch(
        lme4::lmer(f_final, data = data, REML = TRUE, control = custom_control),
        error = function(e) {
          progress_log(sprintf("[Final] REML refit failed: %s; retaining ML fit.",
                               conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
          NULL
        }
      )
      if (!is.null(m_final_reml)) {
        existing_attrs <- attributes(m_final)[c("step4_selected",
                                                "step4_lrt_table")]
        for (an in names(existing_attrs)) {
          if (!is.null(existing_attrs[[an]])) {
            attr(m_final_reml, an) <- existing_attrs[[an]]
          }
        }
        m_final <- m_final_reml
      }
    }
  }
  
  # ---- Mandatory final-model validation. ----
  # Keep derivative-free fits during selection, then refit the exact selected
  # formula with derivatives before any inference, output, or serialization.
  progress_log("[Final] Refitting exact LMM formula with derivatives enabled.",
               indent = 1)
  m_final <- refit_and_validate_final_lmm(m_final, data)
  diag_log$final_validation <- attr(m_final, "final_validation")
  diag_log$final_random_tier <- attr(m_final, "final_random_tier")
  diag_log$step5_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_final)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Final] Acceptance gate: %s",
                       format_final_lmm_diagnostics(diag_log$final_validation)),
               indent = 1)

  # ---- Defensive lmerTest class upgrade. ----
  # 
  # CRITICAL for Satterthwaite/KR p-values. When fit via lme4::lmer() (rather
  # than lmerTest::lmer()), the resulting object has class "lmerMod" only.
  # Calling anova(model, ddf="Satterthwaite") on a bare lmerMod does NOT
  # dispatch to lmerTest's S4 method; lme4's base anova() handles it,
  # silently ignoring the ddf argument and returning a table with F values
  # but NO Pr(>F) and NO NumDF/DenDF columns. The downstream cascade then
  # detects "no Pr column" and falls through to Wald.
  # 
  # The fix is to upgrade the class via lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest() (a
  # free no-refit operation that registers the model with lmerTest's
  # df-computation machinery). buildmer internally fits via lmerTest::lmer()
  # so its @model output may already be lmerModLmerTest; but our 
  # add_correlations_step4 refits via lme4::lmer() in many paths, losing the
  # lmerTest class. This guard ensures the final returned model is dispatch-
  # ready regardless of which fallback path was taken.
  if (inherits(m_final, "merMod") && !inherits(m_final, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
    m_final_lt <- tryCatch(
      lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(m_final),
      error = function(e) {
        progress_log(sprintf("[Final] lmerTest class upgrade failed: %s",
                             conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (!is.null(m_final_lt)) {
      existing_attrs <- attributes(m_final)[c(
        "step4_selected", "step4_lrt_table", "final_validation",
        "final_random_tier"
      )]
      for (an in names(existing_attrs)) {
        if (!is.null(existing_attrs[[an]])) {
          attr(m_final_lt, an) <- existing_attrs[[an]]
        }
      }
      m_final <- m_final_lt
      progress_log("[Final] LMM upgraded to lmerModLmerTest for Satt/KR dispatch.",
                   indent = 1)
    }
  }
  
  attr(m_final, "bates_diag") <- diag_log
  m_final
}
```


``` {r stage1-runner}
# ==============================================================================
# 5. Stage 1 Runner: fit, decompose, and report for one ERP component.
#    Replaces the original run_regression_analysis function.
# ==============================================================================
run_stage1_component <- function(data, erp_name, out_dir, exp_version) {
  
  comp_dir <- file.path(out_dir, erp_name)
  if (!dir.exists(comp_dir)) dir.create(comp_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  
  progress_log(sprintf(">>> Component: %s [%s] (N_subj = %d, N_trial = %d)",
                       erp_name, exp_version,
                       dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id), nrow(data)))
  
  # ---- Fit Stage 1 model via Bates 5-step pipeline. ----
  FINAL_MODEL <- fit_stage1_bates(data, erp_name)
  diag_log <- attr(FINAL_MODEL, "bates_diag")
  
  formula_str <- paste(deparse(formula(FINAL_MODEL)), collapse = " ")
  progress_log(sprintf("[Final model] %s", stringr::str_squish(formula_str)), indent = 1)
  
  # ---- Type III ANOVA: cascade Satterthwaite -> Kenward-Roger -> Wald. ----
  # 
  # CASCADE: lmerTest cascade for LMM.
  #   (1) Satterthwaite F  - lmerTest::anova; preferred (Luke 2017).
  #   (2) Kenward-Roger F  - pbkrtest backend; conservative fallback,
  #       different numerical implementation than Satterthwaite.
  #   (3) Wald chi-square  - car::Anova; last resort, asymptotic.
  # 
  # The cascade is necessary because lmerTest's Satt/KR dispatch requires
  # the model to have class "lmerModLmerTest" (not bare "lmerMod"). The
  # fit_stage1_bates engine upgrades the class before returning, but a
  # second defensive upgrade here protects against models loaded from
  # disk via readRDS or any other path bypassing the engine guard.
  progress_log("[ANOVA] Computing Type III tests...", indent = 1)
  t_anova <- Sys.time()
  
  # Defensive class upgrade. See fit_stage1_bates for full rationale.
  if (inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "merMod") &&
      !inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
    FINAL_MODEL_lt <- tryCatch(
      lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(FINAL_MODEL),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (!is.null(FINAL_MODEL_lt)) FINAL_MODEL <- FINAL_MODEL_lt
  }
  
  anova_res <- NULL
  method_used <- NA_character_
  
  # Attempt 1: Satterthwaite.
  anova_res <- tryCatch({
    res <- suppressWarnings(anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
    if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
      method_used <- "Satterthwaite_F"
      res
    } else {
      progress_log("[ANOVA] Satterthwaite returned no p-value column; trying Kenward-Roger.",
                   indent = 2)
      NULL
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] Satterthwaite errored (%s); trying Kenward-Roger.",
                         conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
    NULL
  })
  
  # Attempt 2: Kenward-Roger.
  if (is.null(anova_res)) {
    anova_res <- tryCatch({
      res <- suppressWarnings(anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, ddf = "Kenward-Roger"))
      if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
        method_used <- "Kenward_Roger_F"
        res
      } else {
        progress_log("[ANOVA] Kenward-Roger returned no p-value column; falling back to Wald.",
                     indent = 2)
        NULL
      }
    }, error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] Kenward-Roger errored (%s); falling back to Wald.",
                           conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
      NULL
    })
  }
  
  # Attempt 3: Wald.
  if (is.null(anova_res)) {
    anova_res <- car::Anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, test.statistic = "Chisq")
    method_used <- "Wald_chi_square"
  }
  
  diag_log$anova_method <- method_used
  progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] Method: %s. Elapsed: %s.",
                       method_used, format_elapsed(t_anova)),
               indent = 2)
  
  anova_apa <- format_anova_apa(anova_res, FINAL_MODEL)
  # Include partial eta-squared with 95% CI in console print so users see
  # effect sizes during long pipeline runs. The full table (with p_val
  # column) is written to anova_apa.md; controlling print width avoids
  # console wrapping.
  print(anova_apa %>% dplyr::select(Effect, APA_Report, eta2_partial_95CI, Sig))
  
  # ---- Post-hoc decomposition (single-factor emotion). ----
  #
  # Face phase has ONE design factor (emotion), so there is no interaction to
  # decompose. The post-hoc of interest is the pairwise comparison among the
  # five emotion levels (FDR-corrected). We tag the table by the omnibus
  # emotion effect: Confirmatory (p < confirmatory_alpha),
  # Exploratory_Marginal (confirmatory_alpha <= p < marginal_threshold), or NS,
  # for transparency. Pairwise comparisons are computed in all cases.
  cat("   [Post-hoc] FDR-corrected emotion pairwise...\n")

  # Extract omnibus emotion p-value defensively (column name varies:
  # 'Pr(>F)' lmerTest, 'Pr(>Chisq)' car::Anova).
  p_emotion <- NA_real_
  if ("emotion" %in% rownames(anova_res)) {
    for (pcol in c("Pr(>F)", "Pr(>Chisq)")) {
      if (pcol %in% colnames(anova_res)) {
        val <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(anova_res["emotion", pcol]))
        if (length(val) == 1 && !is.na(val)) { p_emotion <- val; break }
      }
    }
  }
  if (is.na(p_emotion)) p_emotion <- 1.0
  status_tag <- if (p_emotion < confirmatory_alpha) "Confirmatory"
                else if (p_emotion < marginal_threshold) "Exploratory_Marginal"
                else "NS"

  # emmeans 'at': hold Baseline_c at its mean (0 after centering) under Alday;
  # nothing to hold under Traditional.
  at_list <- if (use_baseline_covariate) list(Baseline_c = 0) else list()

  # Helper: emmeans pairs with explicit infer=c(TRUE,TRUE) so summary() returns
  # BOTH CI columns AND p.value (format_posthoc_apa requires both).
  pairs_with_ci <- function(emm, ...) {
    summary(pairs(emm, ...), infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
  }

  list_of_tables <- list(
    "ANOVA_Main" = anova_apa,
    "Model_Formula" = data.frame(Formula = formula_str),
    "Model_Coefficients" = format_coefs(FINAL_MODEL)
  )
  list_of_supp_tables <- list()

  progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc] emotion omnibus p = %.4f -> %s; pairwise (FDR)...",
                       p_emotion, status_tag), indent = 1)
  t_me <- Sys.time()
  emo_pairs <- format_posthoc_apa(
    pairs_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ emotion, at = at_list), adjust = "fdr")
  )
  emo_pairs$Status <- status_tag
  list_of_tables[["Main_Effect_Emotion"]] <- emo_pairs
  progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc emotion] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_me)), indent = 3)

  progress_log("[Descriptive] estimated marginal means...", indent = 2)
  t_me <- Sys.time()
  list_of_tables[["Descriptive_Means"]] <- beautify_labels(kill_scipen(
    as.data.frame(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ emotion, at = at_list))
  ))
  progress_log(sprintf("[Descriptive] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_me)), indent = 3)
  
  # ---- Reporting Layer (replaces multi-sheet Excel as primary output). ----
  
  # Component status (confirmatory vs exploratory) for downstream filtering.
  comp_status <- component_status(erp_name)
  
  # 1. REPRODUCIBILITY metadata.
  sink(file.path(comp_dir, "REPRODUCIBILITY.txt"))
  cat("# Reproducibility log for ERP component:", erp_name, "\n")
  cat("# Generated:", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n\n")
  write_input_provenance(input_provenance)
  cat("## Status: ", comp_status, "\n\n")
  cat("## Final formula:\n")
  cat(formula_str, "\n\n")
  cat("## Software versions:\n")
  cat("R:        ", R.version.string, "\n")
  cat("lme4:     ", as.character(packageVersion("lme4")), "\n")
  cat("lmerTest: ", as.character(packageVersion("lmerTest")), "\n")
  cat("pbkrtest: ", as.character(packageVersion("pbkrtest")), "\n")
  cat("buildmer: ", as.character(packageVersion("buildmer")), "\n")
  cat("emmeans:  ", as.character(packageVersion("emmeans")), "\n\n")
  cat("## Convergence diagnostics:\n")
  final_validation <- attr(FINAL_MODEL, "final_validation") %||%
    final_lmm_diagnostics(FINAL_MODEL)
  cat("Acceptance gate passed:", final_validation$valid, "\n")
  cat("Optimizer:              bobyqa\n")
  cat("Optimizer code:        ", final_validation$optimizer_code, "\n")
  cat("Convergence messages:  ",
      ifelse(nchar(final_validation$convergence_messages) == 0,
             "none", final_validation$convergence_messages), "\n")
  cat("Singular fit:          ", final_validation$singular, "\n")
  cat("Hessian available:     ", final_validation$hessian_available, "\n")
  cat("Hessian positive-definite:", final_validation$hessian_positive_definite, "\n")
  cat("Finite fixed-effect SE:", final_validation$finite_fixed_se, "\n")
  cat("Finite likelihood/AIC: ", final_validation$finite_likelihood, "\n")
  cat("Final random tier:     ",
      attr(FINAL_MODEL, "final_random_tier") %||% "selected_formula", "\n")
  cat("REML:         TRUE\n")
  cat("Observations:", nobs(FINAL_MODEL), "\n")
  cat("Subjects:    ", lme4::ngrps(FINAL_MODEL)["participant_id"], "\n\n")
  cat("## Bates 5-step diagnostic log:\n")
  cat("Term ordering criterion:     LRT (default)\n")
  cat("Term elimination criterion:  LRTalpha(0.20) (Matuschek et al., 2017)\n")
  cat("Random contrast columns:     ",
      paste(diag_log$random_contrast_columns %||% character(0), collapse = ", "),
      "\n")
  cat("Random slope blocks:         ",
      paste(diag_log$random_slope_blocks %||% character(0), collapse = ", "),
      "\n")
  cat("Step 1 (Maximal):           ", diag_log$step1_status, "\n")
  if (!is.null(diag_log$step1_pca)) {
    cat("  Step 1 effective/nominal: ",
        count_effective_dims(diag_log$step1_pca), "/",
        nrow(diag_log$step1_pca), "\n")
  }
  cat("Step 2 (ZCP):               ", diag_log$step2_status, "\n")
  cat("Step 3 (LRT reduction):     ", diag_log$step3_final_formula, "\n")
  cat("Step 4 (correlations):      ", diag_log$step4_status, "\n")
  cat("Step 5 (final dims):        ",
      count_effective_dims(diag_log$step5_pca), "/",
      nrow(diag_log$step5_pca), "\n")
  cat("\n## Inferential method:\n")
  cat("ANOVA test:                 ", diag_log$anova_method %||% "Wald_chi_square",
      "\n")
  if (identical(diag_log$anova_method, "Kenward_Roger_F")) {
    cat("Note: Satterthwaite returned no p-value column; Kenward-Roger\n")
    cat("(pbkrtest backend) used as second-tier method. Both Satt and KR\n")
    cat("are finite-DenDF F approximations; KR is more conservative.\n")
  }
  if (identical(diag_log$anova_method, "Wald_chi_square")) {
    cat("Note: Both Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger failed (no p-value\n")
    cat("column or error). Wald chi-square (car::Anova) used as final\n")
    cat("fallback. Wald is anti-conservative for finite N (Luke 2017),\n")
    cat("interpret reported p-values with caution.\n")
  }
  sink()
  
  # 2. saveRDS for offline re-analysis (Methods replication, sensitivity).
  saveRDS(FINAL_MODEL,
          file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("final_model_%s.rds", erp_name)))
  
  # 3. Full model summary (Alday-style transparency).
  sink(file.path(comp_dir, "summary_text.txt"))
  print(summary(FINAL_MODEL))
  sink()
  
  # 4. ANOVA table in markdown (manuscript-ready).
  writeLines(
    knitr::kable(anova_apa, format = "markdown",
                 caption = sprintf("Type III ANOVA (%s), %s.",
                                   diag_log$anova_method %||% "Wald", erp_name)),
    con = file.path(comp_dir, "anova_apa.md")
  )
  
  # 5. R-squared (Nakagawa & Schielzeth, 2013).
  r2_obj <- tryCatch(performance::r2(FINAL_MODEL), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(r2_obj)) {
    r2_df <- data.frame(
      R2_marginal    = r2_obj$R2_marginal,
      R2_conditional = r2_obj$R2_conditional
    )
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(kill_scipen(r2_df), format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Nakagawa & Schielzeth R\u00B2, %s.", erp_name)),
      con = file.path(comp_dir, "r2.md")
    )
  }

  # 5b. LMM residual-assumption diagnostics (Meteyard & Davies 2020, Table 7
  # "Assumptions"). Best-effort; never blocks the analysis.
  tryCatch(lmm_assumption_diagnostics(FINAL_MODEL, erp_name, comp_dir),
           error = function(e) NULL)

  # 6. Post-hoc tables in markdown (one file per contrast type).
  # Confirmatory tables go to comp_dir; marginal tables go to Supplementary.
  for (nm in names(list_of_tables)) {
    safe_nm <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", nm)
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(list_of_tables[[nm]], format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("%s -- %s", erp_name, nm)),
      con = file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("posthoc_%s.md", safe_nm))
    )
  }
  
  if (length(list_of_supp_tables) > 0) {
    supp_comp_dir <- file.path(out_suppl,
                               sprintf("%s_marginal_contrasts", erp_name))
    if (!dir.exists(supp_comp_dir)) dir.create(supp_comp_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    for (nm in names(list_of_supp_tables)) {
      safe_nm <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", nm)
      writeLines(
        knitr::kable(list_of_supp_tables[[nm]], format = "markdown",
                     caption = sprintf("%s -- %s [MARGINAL: 0.05<=p<0.10]",
                                       erp_name, nm)),
        con = file.path(supp_comp_dir, sprintf("posthoc_%s.md", safe_nm))
      )
    }
  }
  
  # 7. Step 4 LRT comparison table (when applicable).
  step4_lrt <- attr(FINAL_MODEL, "step4_lrt_table")
  if (!is.null(step4_lrt) && nrow(step4_lrt) > 0) {
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(kill_scipen(step4_lrt), format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Step 4 candidate-correlation LRT, %s.", erp_name)),
      con = file.path(comp_dir, "step4_correlation_lrt.md")
    )
  }
  
  # 8. Bates rePCA summary in markdown (Step 5 documentation).
  if (!is.null(diag_log$step5_pca) && !all(is.na(diag_log$step5_pca$component))) {
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(kill_scipen(diag_log$step5_pca), format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Final-model rePCA dimensionality, %s.", erp_name)),
      con = file.path(comp_dir, "step5_rePCA.md")
    )
  }
  
  # 9. Excel export (legacy compatibility for non-markdown workflows).
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  for (sheet_name in names(list_of_tables)) {
    safe_sheet <- substr(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", sheet_name), 1, 31)
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, safe_sheet)
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, safe_sheet, list_of_tables[[sheet_name]])
    openxlsx::addStyle(wb, safe_sheet,
      openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", border = "Bottom"),
      rows = 1, cols = 1:ncol(list_of_tables[[sheet_name]]))
  }
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb,
    file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("STATS_%s_%s.xlsx", exp_version, erp_name)),
    overwrite = TRUE)
  
  # ---- Visualization Layer. ----
  cat("   [Visualization]\n")
  try({
    p_forest <- sjPlot::plot_model(FINAL_MODEL, type = "est",
                                   show.values = TRUE, show.p = TRUE,
                                   title = sprintf("%s [%s] coefficients",
                                                   erp_name, exp_version)) + theme_bw()
    ggsave(file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("Forest_%s_%s.pdf", exp_version, erp_name)),
           p_forest, width = 7, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)
  })
  
  try({
    pd <- as.data.frame(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, ~ emotion, at = at_list))
    p_emm <- ggplot(pd, aes(x = emotion, y = emmean, fill = emotion)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = emmean - SE, ymax = emmean + SE), width = 0.2) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = colors_emo, labels = labels_emo, guide = "none") +
      scale_x_discrete(labels = labels_emo) +
      labs(title = sprintf("%s %s: emotion main effect", exp_version, erp_name),
           y = "Amplitude (\u00B5V)", x = "Facial expression")
    ggsave(file.path(comp_dir, sprintf("Plot_%s_%s.pdf", exp_version, erp_name)),
           p_emm, width = 7, height = 5, device = cairo_pdf)
  })
  
  cat("   >>> Component complete.\n")
  invisible(FINAL_MODEL)
}

# ==============================================================================
# Multi-component side-by-side table for manuscript supplementary.
# Mirrors the convention of presenting all ERP components in a single tab_model
# HTML which can be opened in Word for final formatting.
# ==============================================================================
report_stage1_multi <- function(model_list, exp_version, out_dir) {
  if (length(model_list) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
  
  out_html <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("Stage1_AllComponents_%s.html", exp_version))
  out_md   <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("Stage1_AllComponents_%s.md", exp_version))
  
  # ---- HTML output via sjPlot::tab_model (preferred for manuscript supplementary) ----
  tab_model_succeeded <- FALSE
  tryCatch({
    sjPlot::tab_model(
      model_list,
      show.se = TRUE, show.stat = TRUE, show.ci = FALSE,
      string.se = "SE", string.stat = "t-value", string.p = "p-value",
      show.re.var = TRUE, show.obs = TRUE, show.icc = FALSE,
      show.r2 = TRUE, show.loglik = TRUE, show.dev = TRUE,
      emph.p = TRUE, p.style = "numeric_stars",
      file = out_html,
      dv.labels = names(model_list)
    )
    # Verify file actually exists. tab_model can silently fail on some sjPlot
    # versions or with mixed-class model lists, returning NULL without writing.
    if (file.exists(out_html) && file.size(out_html) > 0) {
      cat(sprintf("[Multi-component HTML] %s\n", basename(out_html)))
      tab_model_succeeded <- TRUE
    } else {
      cat(sprintf("[WARN] tab_model returned without error but no file written: %s\n",
                  out_html))
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[WARN] tab_model failed: %s\n", conditionMessage(e)))
  })
  
  # ---- Markdown fallback: assemble a side-by-side ANOVA table ----
  # Always produced, regardless of tab_model success. Provides a
  # version-independent manuscript-ready table that can be pasted into Word.
  tryCatch({
    rows <- list()
    methods_log <- character(0)
    for (comp_name in names(model_list)) {
      mdl <- model_list[[comp_name]]
      
      # Defensive class upgrade. Mirrors the upgrade in fit_stage1_bates;
      # protects against models loaded directly from RDS without going
      # through the engine.
      if (inherits(mdl, "merMod") && !inherits(mdl, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
        mdl_upgraded <- tryCatch(
          lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(mdl),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
        if (!is.null(mdl_upgraded)) mdl <- mdl_upgraded
      }
      
      # Per-component cascade: Satt -> KR -> Wald.
      anova_obj <- NULL
      method_used <- NA_character_
      
      # Attempt 1: Satterthwaite.
      anova_obj <- tryCatch({
        res <- suppressWarnings(anova(mdl, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
        if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
          method_used <- "Satterthwaite F"
          res
        } else {
          NULL
        }
      }, error = function(e) NULL)
      
      # Attempt 2: Kenward-Roger.
      if (is.null(anova_obj)) {
        anova_obj <- tryCatch({
          res <- suppressWarnings(anova(mdl, type = 3, ddf = "Kenward-Roger"))
          if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
            method_used <- "Kenward-Roger F"
            res
          } else {
            NULL
          }
        }, error = function(e) NULL)
      }
      
      # Attempt 3: Wald.
      if (is.null(anova_obj)) {
        anova_obj <- tryCatch(
          car::Anova(mdl, type = 3, test.statistic = "Chisq"),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
        if (!is.null(anova_obj)) method_used <- "Wald chi-square (LMM fallback)"
      }
      
      if (is.null(anova_obj)) next
      
      methods_log <- c(methods_log, sprintf("%s: %s", comp_name, method_used))
      
      apa <- format_anova_apa(anova_obj, mdl)
      apa$Component <- comp_name
      apa$Status    <- component_status(comp_name)
      apa$Method    <- method_used
      rows[[comp_name]] <- apa[, c("Component", "Status", "Effect",
                                   "APA_Report", "eta2_partial_95CI",
                                   "Sig", "Method")]
    }
    
    if (length(rows) > 0) {
      combined <- do.call(rbind, rows)
      writeLines(
        c(sprintf("# Stage 1 ANOVA Summary, %s", exp_version),
          sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
          "",
          "Type III ANOVA tests. LMM analyses use a Satterthwaite -> ",
          "Kenward-Roger -> Wald cascade (lmerTest, pbkrtest, car). All EEG",
          "analyses are LMM (Gaussian on amplitude); GLMM is not used.",
          "Component Status indicates confirmatory vs exploratory face-locked",
          "components (a reporting-layer label set in the face component config).",
          "",
          "## Methods used per component:",
          paste0("- ", methods_log),
          "",
          knitr::kable(combined, format = "markdown",
                       caption = sprintf("Stage 1 fixed-effect tests across %d ERP components.",
                                         length(rows)))),
        con = out_md
      )
      cat(sprintf("[Multi-component Markdown] %s\n", basename(out_md)))
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[WARN] Markdown multi-component summary failed: %s\n",
                conditionMessage(e)))
  })
  
  invisible(list(html_ok = tab_model_succeeded, html_path = out_html, md_path = out_md))
}
```

``` {r execution}
# ==============================================================================
# 7. Execution Phase
# ==============================================================================
path_pipeline <- here("data", paste0("02_Pipeline_Output_", experiment_version))
# Face-locked single-trial table from the method-specific Face_Locked dir
# (method_dir set by the use_baseline_correction toggle in setup).
path_stim <- file.path(path_pipeline, method_dir, "Face_Locked", "trials.csv")

path_cov_base <- file.path(path_pipeline, "Covariates")
path_cov_candidates <- c(
  file.path(path_cov_base, sprintf("SVO_PID5BF_PostRating_%s.csv", experiment_version)),
  file.path(path_cov_base, sprintf("SVO_PID5BF_PostRating_%s.xlsx", experiment_version)),
  file.path(path_cov_base, "SVO_PID5BF_PostRating.csv"),
  file.path(path_cov_base, "SVO_PID5BF_PostRating.xlsx")
)

path_cov <- NA_character_
for (cand in path_cov_candidates) {
  if (file.exists(cand)) { path_cov <- cand; break }
}

if (is.na(path_cov)) warning("No covariate file found; Stage 2 will be skipped.")
if (!file.exists(path_stim)) {
  stop(sprintf("Stimulus file not found: %s\nVerify upstream preprocessing.", path_stim))
}
input_provenance <- capture_canonical_input(
  path_stim,
  sprintf("%s face phase (%s)", experiment_version, method_dir),
  file.path("data", paste0("02_Pipeline_Output_", experiment_version),
            method_dir, "Face_Locked", "trials.csv")
)

cat("--- Loading Covariates ---\n")
df_covs <- load_covariates(path_cov)

# ---- Stage 1: stimulus-locked components ----
stage1_models <- list()
# stage1_data holds per-component trial-level data, used by the Track C rating
# control model. Initialised at outer scope so downstream chunks can test
# length(stage1_data) > 0 unconditionally.
stage1_data <- list()

if (file.exists(path_stim)) {
  progress_log("=== Processing Stimulus-Locked Components ===")
  total_stim <- length(analyze_stim_components)
  pipeline_t0 <- Sys.time()
  
  for (comp_idx in seq_along(analyze_stim_components)) {
    comp_name <- analyze_stim_components[comp_idx]
    progress_log(sprintf(">>> [%d/%d] Component: %s [%s] (cumulative: %s)",
                         comp_idx, total_stim, comp_name,
                         component_status(comp_name),
                         format_elapsed(pipeline_t0)))
    baseline_col_name <- paste0("Baseline_", comp_name)
    df_comp <- load_and_prep(path_stim, df_covs, comp_name, baseline_col_name)
    
    if (!is.null(df_comp)) {
      check_uniqueness(df_comp, comp_name)
      
      # Baseline balance pre-check (diagnostic only; does not gate analysis).
      # Output to Supplementary/baseline_balance/<component>_baseline_balance.md.
      pre_check_baseline_balance(
        data     = df_comp,
        comp_name = comp_name,
        out_dir   = file.path(out_suppl, "baseline_balance")
      )
      
      fit <- run_stage1_component(df_comp, comp_name, out_stage1, experiment_version)
      
      if (!is.null(fit)) {
        stage1_models[[comp_name]] <- fit
        stage1_data[[comp_name]]   <- df_comp  # retained for Track C rating control
      }
    }
    progress_log(sprintf(">>> [%d/%d] %s complete.", comp_idx, total_stim, comp_name))
  }
}

# Note: response-locked components (formerly CPP) removed in v2 as out of
# scope for the offer-phase analysis. Pipeline now processes only stimulus-
# locked components. To restore CPP analysis, re-introduce response-locked
# block above with explicit baseline merge from the stimulus-locked file.

# ---- Multi-component side-by-side table for manuscript supplementary ----
report_stage1_multi(stage1_models, experiment_version, out_tables)

cat(sprintf("\n[Stage 1 complete] Fitted %d/%d components.\n",
            length(stage1_models),
            length(analyze_stim_components)))
```

``` {r execution-stage2}
# ==============================================================================
# 8. Stage 2 Execution (EEG: rating nuisance-covariate control only)
# ==============================================================================
# Trait moderation (SVO + Negative Affectivity + PID5BF+) and the BLUP screen
# have moved out of the EEG to the behavioral analysis. The only EEG Stage 2 step
# is the rating nuisance-covariate control (Rating_1/2/3 as grand-mean-centered
# main effects); run_covariate_control_check(), called below.
# ==============================================================================

# Stage 2 (EEG) is now only the rating nuisance-covariate control; trait
# moderation moved to the behavioral analysis.
# Stage 2 runs only under the Alday method (run_stage2 == TRUE). In the
# Traditional sensitivity analysis it is deliberately disabled: BLUPs/moderation
# from traditional baseline subtraction reflect a different latent quantity than
# the Alday baseline-as-covariate estimates and are not directly comparable; the
# sensitivity analysis exists to verify Stage 1 fixed-effect conclusions, not to
# re-analyse individual differences (and re-running would inflate the FDR family).
if (!run_stage2) {
  dir.create(out_stage2, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  writeLines(c(
    "# Stage 2 (Trait Moderation): DELIBERATELY DISABLED",
    sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
    "",
    "This is the TRADITIONAL baseline-subtraction SENSITIVITY analysis",
    "(use_baseline_correction = TRUE). Stage 2 individual-difference analysis",
    "is intentionally not run here, for three reasons:",
    "",
    "1. Estimates from traditional baseline subtraction reflect a different",
    "   latent quantity than the Alday baseline-as-covariate estimates;",
    "   the two are not directly comparable.",
    "2. The sensitivity analysis exists to verify the Stage 1 fixed-effect",
    "   conclusions, not to re-analyse individual differences.",
    "3. Re-running Stage 2 would double the FDR-adjusted family count with no",
    "   interpretable gain.",
    "",
    "For the primary Stage 2 results see the Alday output tree",
    "(results/EEG/FacePhase_E1/Bates_Alday/Stage2_TraitModeration/)."
  ), file.path(out_stage2, "STAGE2_DISABLED_README.md"))
  cat("\n[Stage 2 disabled] Traditional sensitivity analysis; wrote STAGE2_DISABLED_README.md\n")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Nuisance-covariate control check (Rating_1/2/3).
# The three cover-story belief ratings are manipulation checks, NOT theoretical
# moderators (decision 2026-06). They enter a SEPARATE control model as grand-
# mean-centered MAIN-EFFECT covariates (no interaction), leaving the primary
# Stage 1 inference untouched. Purpose: confirm the design effect(s) are robust
# to controlling for belief strength, and report each rating's main-effect
# association with amplitude. Output: Stage2_TraitModeration/Covariate_Control_Ratings/.
# `design_rhs` is the design portion of the fixed effects ("emotion" here; the
# offer-phase script passes "emotion * offer_type").
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
run_covariate_control_check <- function(stage1_models, stage1_data, df_traits,
                                        rating_covs, out_dir,
                                        design_rhs = "emotion") {
  if (is.null(df_traits) || length(stage1_models) == 0) {
    cat("[Covariate control] No models or covariates; skipping.\n"); return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  available <- intersect(rating_covs, names(df_traits))
  if (length(available) == 0) {
    cat("[Covariate control] No rating covariates in covariate file; skipping.\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("\n=== Stage 2C: Ratings as nuisance covariates (control model) ===\n"))
  cat(sprintf("[Covariate control] Ratings: %s\n", paste(available, collapse = ", ")))

  for (comp_name in names(stage1_models)) {
    m1   <- stage1_models[[comp_name]]
    df_c <- stage1_data[[comp_name]]
    if (is.null(m1) || is.null(df_c)) next
    rating_random_design <- add_random_contrast_columns(
      df_c, "emotion", "participant_id"
    )
    df_c <- rating_random_design$data

    f_stage1  <- stats::formula(m1)
    response  <- as.character(f_stage1[[2L]])
    re_terms  <- lme4::findbars(f_stage1)
    re_string <- if (length(re_terms) > 0)
      paste0("(", sapply(re_terms, deparse), ")", collapse = " + ")
    else "(1 | participant_id)"

    # Grand-mean center each available rating present in this component's data.
    rating_terms <- c()
    for (rc in available) {
      if (!rc %in% names(df_c)) next
      cc <- paste0(rc, "_c")
      df_c[[cc]] <- df_c[[rc]] - mean(df_c[[rc]], na.rm = TRUE)
      rating_terms <- c(rating_terms, cc)
    }
    if (length(rating_terms) == 0) {
      cat(sprintf("  [%s] no rating columns present; skipping.\n", comp_name)); next
    }
    n_primary <- nrow(df_c)
    df_c <- df_c[stats::complete.cases(df_c[, rating_terms, drop = FALSE]), ]
    if (nrow(df_c) == 0) next
    n_ctrl      <- nrow(df_c)
    n_subj_ctrl <- length(unique(df_c$participant_id))
    n_msg <- if (n_primary == n_ctrl)
      sprintf("N: %d trials (%d subjects), identical to the primary Stage 1 model -- no rows dropped for missing ratings.",
              n_ctrl, n_subj_ctrl)
    else
      sprintf("N: %d -> %d trials (%d subjects) after dropping subjects with missing ratings; the robustness comparison is therefore NOT strictly same-N relative to the primary model.",
              n_primary, n_ctrl, n_subj_ctrl)

    baseline_term <- if ("Baseline_c" %in% all.vars(f_stage1)) " + Baseline_c" else ""
    f_ctrl <- stats::as.formula(sprintf(
      "%s ~ %s + %s%s + %s", response, design_rhs,
      paste(rating_terms, collapse = " + "), baseline_term, re_string))

    comp_dir <- file.path(out_dir, comp_name)
    if (!dir.exists(comp_dir)) dir.create(comp_dir, recursive = TRUE)
    fit_result <- tryCatch(
      list(
        model = suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
          lmerTest::lmer(
            f_ctrl, data = df_c, REML = TRUE,
            control = custom_control_final
          )
        )),
        error = NULL
      ),
      error = function(e) list(model = NULL, error = conditionMessage(e))
    )
    fit <- fit_result$model
    if (is.null(fit)) {
      writeLines(c(
        sprintf("# Nuisance-covariate control (Ratings): %s", comp_name),
        sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
        "", "Status: FAILED", sprintf("Model: %s", paste(deparse(f_ctrl), collapse = " ")),
        sprintf("Reason: fitting error: %s", fit_result$error)
      ), file.path(comp_dir, "covariate_control.md"))
      cat(sprintf("  [%s] control model failed: %s\n", comp_name, fit_result$error))
      next
    }
    fit_diag <- final_lmm_diagnostics(fit)
    if (!isTRUE(fit_diag$valid)) {
      writeLines(c(
        sprintf("# Nuisance-covariate control (Ratings): %s", comp_name),
        sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
        "", "Status: FAILED", sprintf("Model: %s", paste(deparse(f_ctrl), collapse = " ")),
        sprintf("Reason: acceptance gate failed: %s",
                format_final_lmm_diagnostics(fit_diag))
      ), file.path(comp_dir, "covariate_control.md"))
      cat(sprintf("  [%s] control model invalid: %s\n", comp_name,
                  format_final_lmm_diagnostics(fit_diag)))
      next
    }
    if (!inherits(fit, "lmerModLmerTest"))
      fit <- tryCatch(lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(fit), error = function(e) fit)

    res <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(anova(fit, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite")),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(res) || !any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res))))
      res <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(anova(fit, type = 3, ddf = "Kenward-Roger")),
                      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(res))
      res <- tryCatch(car::Anova(fit, type = 3, test.statistic = "Chisq"), error = function(e) NULL)

    anova_apa <- if (!is.null(res)) format_anova_apa(res, fit) else NULL
    coefs <- tryCatch(format_coefs(fit), error = function(e) NULL)

    writeLines(c(
      sprintf("# Nuisance-covariate control (Ratings): %s", comp_name),
      sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
      "",
      "Status: PASSED",
      sprintf("Acceptance diagnostics: %s", format_final_lmm_diagnostics(fit_diag)),
      "",
      sprintf("Model: %s", paste(deparse(f_ctrl), collapse = " ")),
      "",
      "Ratings (Rating_1/2/3) are subject-level (between-subjects) cover-story",
      "belief checks, entered as grand-mean-centered MAIN-EFFECT nuisance",
      "covariates (no interaction). NOTE: a purely between-subjects covariate is",
      "(in expectation) orthogonal to the within-subject emotion contrast, so it",
      "can only absorb between-subjects variance in the intercept and cannot, by",
      "construction, materially alter the within-subject emotion effect. This",
      "model therefore (i) confirms the within-subject effect is not carried by",
      "between-subjects belief differences, and (ii) reports each rating's main-",
      "effect association with overall amplitude. It is NOT a moderation test and",
      "does NOT 'control away a confound' of the focal effect; the primary",
      "Stage 1 inference is unchanged.",
      "",
      n_msg,
      "",
      "## Type III ANOVA (design effects controlling for ratings)",
      if (!is.null(anova_apa)) knitr::kable(anova_apa, format = "markdown", row.names = FALSE) else "ANOVA failed.",
      "",
      "## Fixed-effect coefficients (incl. rating covariates)",
      if (!is.null(coefs)) knitr::kable(coefs, format = "markdown", row.names = FALSE) else "Coefficient extraction failed."
    ), file.path(comp_dir, "covariate_control.md"))
    cat(sprintf("  [%s] control model done.\n", comp_name))
  }
  invisible(out_dir)
}

# ---- Track C: Ratings as nuisance covariates (main-effect control model) ----
if (run_stage2 && length(stage1_models) > 0 && length(stage1_data) > 0 && !is.null(df_covs)) {
  run_covariate_control_check(
    stage1_models = stage1_models,
    stage1_data   = stage1_data,
    df_traits     = df_covs,
    rating_covs   = rating_covariates,
    out_dir       = out_stage2_covctrl,
    design_rhs    = "emotion"   # face phase: emotion is the sole design factor
  )
} else {
  cat("\n[Stage 2C skipped] Insufficient inputs for covariate-control model.\n")
}

# Aggregate handle for downstream chunks. EEG Stage 2 produces only the rating
# control model; trait moderation has moved to the behavioral analysis.
stage2_results <- list(covariate_control = "ratings_only")
```

``` {r methods-paragraph}
# ==============================================================================
# 8.5 Methods Paragraph Generation
#
# Auto-generated manuscript Methods text based on the runtime configuration of
# this analysis (component lists, exact package versions, sample N, cascade
# methods used). The paragraph tracks the actual code path; if upstream
# settings change, regenerating this file ensures the manuscript stays in
# sync with the analysis.
#
# Rationale for auto-generation: hand-writing Methods invites drift between
# script and prose. Reviewers increasingly expect such drift to surface, and
# JASP/JAMOVI-style auto-generated Methods text is an emerging norm.
# ==============================================================================

methods_path <- file.path(out_tables,
                          sprintf("Methods_paragraph_%s.md", experiment_version))

# Component count summaries.
n_confirmatory <- length(confirmatory_components)
n_exploratory  <- length(exploratory_components)

confirmatory_str <- paste(confirmatory_components, collapse = ", ")
exploratory_str  <- if (n_exploratory > 0) {
  paste(exploratory_components, collapse = ", ")
} else {
  "none"
}

# Sample summary from the first available stage1 model.
sample_n_subj  <- NA_integer_
sample_n_trial <- NA_integer_
if (length(stage1_models) > 0) {
  first_model <- stage1_models[[1]]
  sample_n_subj  <- as.integer(lme4::ngrps(first_model)["participant_id"])
  sample_n_trial <- as.integer(nobs(first_model))
}

# Design description (face-locked, E1 only).
design_desc <- paste(
  "Experiment 1 used a sequential design in which the proposer's face was",
  "presented before the offer. The present analysis is FACE-LOCKED: ERPs are",
  "time-locked to face onset, at which point the upcoming offer has not yet",
  "been shown. Emotion (five facial expressions: neutral, affiliative,",
  "disgust, dominance, reward) is therefore the sole experimental factor;",
  "offer fairness is not a factor at face onset and is not modeled. This",
  "face-locked analysis is reported as supplementary to the offer-locked",
  "analyses.")

# Method-dependent framing (Alday baseline-as-covariate vs traditional
# subtraction), spliced into the writeLines vector below (c() flattens).
if (use_baseline_covariate) {
  baseline_para <- c(
    "Single-trial ERP amplitudes were analyzed using the Alday (2019)",
    "baseline-as-covariate framework, in which baseline amplitude is fitted",
    "as a fixed-effect covariate rather than subtracted from the epoch. This",
    "is the PRIMARY face-phase analysis. Baseline amplitude was mean-centered",
    "(per Alday 2019) but kept on the microvolt scale.")
  fixed_spec_para <- c(
    "### Fixed-effect specification (Alday)",
    "",
    "For each component the fixed-effect search space was the pairwise model",
    "amplitude ~ (emotion + Baseline_c)^2. The core terms emotion and",
    "Baseline_c were forced to be retained via buildmer's 'include' argument;",
    "the emotion:Baseline_c interaction was subjected to LRT-based inclusion",
    "testing within the same buildmer call.")
  stage2_para <- c(
    "### Stage 2: rating nuisance-covariate control",
    "",
    "Trait moderation (SVO, Negative Affectivity, and the PID5BF+ personality",
    "domains) is NOT run on the face-locked EEG; it has moved to the behavioral",
    "analysis, where these individual differences are examined as per-experiment",
    "main-effect predictors of accept/reject and RT (a between-subjects trait by",
    "within-subjects emotion interaction is anticonservative and underpowered at",
    "n = 30 on single-trial ERPs).",
    "",
    "The only EEG Stage 2 step retained (Alday analysis only) is a control for the",
    "three cover-story belief ratings (Rating_1/2/3), subject-level manipulation",
    "checks entered as grand-mean-centered MAIN-EFFECT NUISANCE COVARIATES (no",
    "interaction) in a separate model. Because these ratings vary only between",
    "participants, they are orthogonal in expectation to the within-subject",
    "emotion contrast and cannot by construction alter it; the model confirms the",
    "emotion effect is not carried by between-subjects belief differences and",
    "reports each rating's main-effect association with amplitude. The primary",
    "Stage 1 inference was left unchanged.")
} else {
  baseline_para <- c(
    "Single-trial ERP amplitudes, baseline-corrected by subtraction of the",
    "mean pre-stimulus interval (-200 to 0 ms) during preprocessing, were",
    "analyzed. This traditional baseline-subtraction analysis is reported as a",
    "SENSITIVITY check on the primary Alday baseline-as-covariate analysis.")
  fixed_spec_para <- c(
    "### Fixed-effect specification (traditional baseline subtraction)",
    "",
    "For each component the fixed-effect model was amplitude ~ emotion. No",
    "baseline covariate is included because baseline was subtracted upstream.")
  stage2_para <- c(
    "### Stage 2",
    "",
    "Stage 2 trait-moderation analysis is deliberately not run in this",
    "traditional baseline-subtraction sensitivity analysis; see",
    "STAGE2_DISABLED_README.md for the rationale.")
}

writeLines(c(
  sprintf("# Methods Paragraph (EEG Single-trial LMM, %s)", experiment_version),
  "",
  sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
  "",
  "## Statistical Analysis",
  "",
  baseline_para,
  "",
  "Mixed-effects models were fitted in R with the lme4",
  sprintf("(%s) and lmerTest (%s) packages.",
          packageVersion("lme4"), packageVersion("lmerTest")),
  "Categorical predictors used sum-to-zero contrasts (R option contr.sum)",
  "to support valid Type III tests in the presence of interactions",
  "(Schad, Vasishth, Hohenstein, & Kliegl, 2020). Trials were excluded",
  "if |amplitude| > 200 microvolts at any electrode (HU pipeline",
  "peak-to-peak rejection, marked as NaN in the single-trial data),",
  "if the participant did not respond (reaction == 0), or if the",
  sprintf("response time fell outside [%d, %d] ms. (Unlike the offer-phase",
          rt_lower_ms, rt_upper_ms),
  "analysis, no 7:3 filler exclusion is applied: the face is identical",
  "regardless of the as-yet-unseen offer, so all emotion trials are valid",
  "face trials.) The response-based criteria were applied at the analysis",
  "layer rather than in upstream",
  "preprocessing, to keep the canonical trials.csv as a single source",
  "of truth and to maintain identical inclusion logic across the",
  "parallel behavioral analysis (Sta_Behaviour_RefAlday.Rmd) and the",
  "Stage 1 EEG analysis reported here.",
  "For each fitted single-trial LMM, residual assumptions were assessed via",
  "residual skewness and excess kurtosis, a homoscedasticity index (the",
  "Spearman correlation between the absolute residual and the fitted value),",
  "and Q-Q and residual-vs-fitted plots (assumptions_<component>.md and .pdf in",
  "each component output directory). At the single-trial sample sizes used",
  "here, formal normality tests are over-powered and were not used for this",
  "purpose.",
  "",
  "### Components and confirmatory framing",
  "",
  design_desc,
  "",
  sprintf("Face-locked components fitted as confirmatory analyses: %s.",
          confirmatory_str),
  sprintf("Face-locked components fitted as exploratory analyses: %s.", exploratory_str),
  "The confirmatory/exploratory label is a reporting-layer distinction",
  "(it sets the FDR family); all components run the identical Stage 1",
  "pipeline. Exploratory components are reported descriptively only.",
  "",
  fixed_spec_para,
  "",
  "### Random-effects structure",
  "",
  "Random-effects structures were selected following the parsimonious-",
  "Bates protocol (Bates, Kliegl, Vasishth, & Baayen, 2015; Matuschek,",
  "Kliegl, Vasishth, Baayen, & Bates, 2017). For each component:",
  "Step 1 specified a maximal model with main-effect random slopes and",
  "full correlations (interaction random slopes were omitted because",
  "cell-level variance components rarely identify in single-trial EEG",
  "with typical N). Step 2 fitted a zero-correlation-parameter (ZCP)",
  "model using separate sum-contrast columns for factor slopes, making",
  "the ZCP variance terms genuinely diagonal. All contrast columns for",
  "one factor were evaluated as one buildmer selection block. Step 3 used buildmer",
  "LRT-based backward elimination at",
  "alpha = 0.20 (Matuschek et al., 2017). Step 4 tested whether adding",
  "correlation parameters improved fit. Step 5 ran rePCA dimensionality",
  "diagnostics to confirm that the final structure was data-supported.",
  "Stimulus identity was counterbalanced via Latin-square design and",
  "was not modeled as a separate random effect (cf. Westfall, Kenny, &",
  "Judd, 2014).",
  "",
  "### Inferential strategy",
  "",
  "Fixed-effect inference used a Type III F-test with denominator",
  "degrees of freedom approximated via a cascading method preference:",
  "Satterthwaite (Kuznetsova, Brockhoff, & Christensen, 2017; Luke,",
  "2017) was attempted first; on numerical failure, Kenward-Roger",
  "(Kenward & Roger, 1997; via the pbkrtest backend) was attempted",
  "next; Wald chi-square (car::Anova) was used only as a final",
  "fallback. The method actually used per component is reported in",
  "supplementary tables. Post-hoc contrasts were computed using emmeans",
  "(Lenth, 2024) with asymptotic standard errors and false-discovery-",
  "rate (FDR) correction within each effect family.",
  "",
  "### Effect-size reporting",
  "",
  "Partial eta-squared with 95% confidence intervals are reported",
  "alongside F-tests (effectsize::eta_squared). Marginal and conditional",
  "R-squared (Nakagawa & Schielzeth, 2013) are reported per component.",
  "All contrast estimates are reported in microvolts with 95% CIs.",
  "",
  "### Post-hoc",
  "",
  "Pairwise comparisons among the five emotion levels (FDR-corrected) were",
  "computed for every component and tagged by the omnibus emotion effect:",
  "Confirmatory (p < 0.05), Exploratory_Marginal (0.05 <= p < 0.10), or NS.",
  "",
  stage2_para,
  "",
  "## Sample",
  "",
  if (!is.na(sample_n_trial) && !is.na(sample_n_subj)) {
    sprintf("%d trials from %d participants entered Stage 1 analysis (%s).",
            sample_n_trial, sample_n_subj, experiment_version)
  } else "Sample size: extraction failed; check stage1_models.",
  "",
  "## References (cite as appropriate)",
  "",
  "Alday, P. M. (2019). How much baseline correction do we need in ERP",
  "  research? Extended GLM model can replace baseline correction while",
  "  lifting its limits. Psychophysiology, 56, e13451.",
  "Bates, D., Kliegl, R., Vasishth, S., & Baayen, R. H. (2015).",
  "  Parsimonious mixed models. arXiv:1506.04967.",
  "Halekoh, U., & Hojsgaard, S. (2014). A Kenward-Roger approximation",
  "  and parametric bootstrap methods for tests in linear mixed models",
  "  -- the R package pbkrtest. Journal of Statistical Software, 59(9).",
  "Kenward, M. G., & Roger, J. H. (1997). Small sample inference for",
  "  fixed effects from restricted maximum likelihood. Biometrics, 53,",
  "  983-997.",
  "Kuznetsova, A., Brockhoff, P. B., & Christensen, R. H. B. (2017).",
  "  lmerTest package: Tests in linear mixed effects models. Journal of",
  "  Statistical Software, 82(13).",
  "Lenth, R. V. (2024). emmeans: Estimated marginal means.",
  "Luke, S. G. (2017). Evaluating significance in linear mixed-effects",
  "  models in R. Behavior Research Methods, 49, 1494-1502.",
  "Matuschek, H., Kliegl, R., Vasishth, S., Baayen, H., & Bates, D.",
  "  (2017). Balancing Type I error and power in linear mixed models.",
  "  Journal of Memory and Language, 94, 305-315.",
  "Nakagawa, S., & Schielzeth, H. (2013). A general and simple method",
  "  for obtaining R^2 from generalized linear mixed-effects models.",
  "  Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 4, 133-142.",
  "Schad, D. J., Vasishth, S., Hohenstein, S., & Kliegl, R. (2020).",
  "  How to capitalize on a priori contrasts in linear (mixed) models.",
  "  Journal of Memory and Language, 110, 104038.",
  "Westfall, J., Kenny, D. A., & Judd, C. M. (2014). Statistical power",
  "  and optimal design in experiments in which samples of participants",
  "  respond to samples of stimuli. Journal of Experimental Psychology:",
  "  General, 143, 2020-2045.",
  "",
  "References added in v2.2 (single-stage moderation rationale):",
  "Hofmann, D. A., & Rovine, M. J. (2007). Multilevel models in",
  "  organizational and management research. In Modern Methods for",
  "  Business Research. Lawrence Erlbaum.",
  "Krueger, R. F., Derringer, J., Markon, K. E., Watson, D., &",
  "  Skodol, A. E. (2012). Initial construction of a maladaptive",
  "  personality trait model and inventory for DSM-5. Psychological",

), methods_path)
```
